recipes.name: Cream of Brie Soup
ingredients_raw: 0.5 pound Brie cheese with the rind, cubed
1 tablespoon green bell pepper, cut into very fine matchsticks
1 tablespoon red bell pepper, cut into very fine matchsticks

steps.text: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add onion and celery; cook until onion is translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in flour and cook for 3 minutes, stirring constantly. Gradually whisk in chicken stock. Simmer until celery is tender, about 20 minutes, stirring occasionally. Stir in Brie cheese and allow to melt for about 5 minutes.

Pour soup into a blender, filling the pitcher no more than halfway full. Hold down the lid of the blender with a folded kitchen towel, then carefully start the blender, using a few quick pulses to get the soup moving before leaving it on to purée. Purée in batches until smooth. Pour into a clean pot. Heat soup to almost simmering over medium-low heat. Pour in cream. To serve, garnish with red and green pepper strips.

raw_recipe.headline: Cream of Brie Soup
raw_recipe.description: This creamy soup with Brie cheese is a rich and delicious treat, whether you choose to ladle it into a regular soup bowl or a warm, toasted bread bowl.

video.description: A fluffy, soft, and flaky delight to have with breakfast. Spread on jam, butter, honey, (or all three!) for a tasty addition to many meals.

review.reviewBody: This is great stuff. Its worth the cost, the effort, the time and you should serve it to someone that has good taste.

I've made this three times now. Each time I used vegetable stock out of preference and white rice flour due to health issues. I tried it with less cream the first time because I was afraid it would be heavy due to the amount of fat in the brie, but it turned out to be lighter than expected. The second and third time I used the whole amount as instructed and in fact, it was lighter than a usual "cream of vegetable" soup. The first time I used a popular industrial brand of brie and it was somewhat bland and somewhat bitter. In my next attempts I used a local, organic brand and found it much tastier and less bitter. The third time I added a large bunch of fresh spinach when sautéing the onions and celery and it is to die for! Thanks so much for sharing your recipe. I would never have thought of this on my own.

I had some Brie that was getting quite mature so I cut off the rind as it was bitter. I didn't have enough celery so I added a carrot, some garlic, herbes de Provence, omitted cream and didn't bothering puréeing. Served with julienned apple and crusty homemade bread. Yummy

This was the epitome of comfort food. The flavor was like a cream of chicken soup with no real flavor of Brie. But in this case that was not a bad thing. I did add some ground nutmeg and cardamom which added to the comfort food experience. Instead of the peppers, I followed the lead of another reviewer and used diced apple and a dollop of hot pepper jam as garnish. My husband actually licked out the bowl with his finger. He has never done this before in my 40 years of cooking for him.

I added garlic, tarragon, thyme, 2 bay leaves, and red pepper flake. I also finished with julienne sliced green apple and some crisped fake bacon (Morning Star Farms) instead of the peppers. They were a great contrast in flavor. It was fantastic! Served it with a green leaf/apple salad with a lemon vinaigrette. Great meal.
I made this following directions but added about 1/4 cup white wine to the chicken broth. This just added a bit of flavor
3.5. Really yummy, but I think it could use more celery. Also used vegetable broth, herbs de provence, garlic powder, tumeric, and salt. served with sliced baguettes.

The soup was very good! I tripled the recipe because I made it for my son and his class that were learning formal dining etiquette in preparation for a formal evening out. My son was bummed he couldn’t eat it all! I guess the ‘formal etiquette’ was to leave some behind. We have leftover so he can eat more and I can have some too! A friend said she added chicken from the main entree and that was really good too.

I love that this recipe uses the beautifully flavorful rind of the Brie. So many recipes direct to trim it off. Cheese makers go to great lengths to make the edible rind an integral part of the eating experience!
Very tasty soup my family loved it

Very easy soup to make. I did use an immersion blender instead of a regular blender and it worked well and soup Did not have to be transferred out of the original pot. I also skipped the red and green peppers as I don’t like them. Next time I make it, I Will remove the Brie rhine. Didn’t like that texture in the soup. Otherwise it was very very tasty and will definitely make again
Fantastic recipe!! Was the star of the dinner party
It’s just perfect as the recipe is written.

Wasn't sure what to expect with this soup - it was like eating melted brie. My husband actually preferred it as a "dip" - thick & creamy. If you like brie, you'll want to try this soup. It's a great base & could go in so many different directions depending on your tastes. Will be making this one again & trying different variations.
Love this soup. Made exactly as described and it was amazing.
